name: Irving at Mile High Vista
award: 2022 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: The Irving at Mile High Vista is a seven-story, all-electric building of 102 affordable apartments (20% to 80% of AMI) at 3270 W. Colfax Ave., built by Urban Land Conservancy with Cho Development on ULC-owned land next to Denver's Corky Gonzales library; it won $1,934,593 a year in federal 4% credit and $1,000,000 in state credit in CHFA's 2022 Round Two and opened in January 2026.
why_it_matters: It shows land banking paying off: ULC bought the site for about $25 a square foot in 2010-2011 with the Denver TOD Fund, held it for over a decade, and contributed the last parcel through a 99-year ground lease with community land trust affordability, layered with Proposition 123 gap money and a city loan.

status.label: Completed and open: grand opening 2026-01-22
status.detail: Ground was broken on 2024-05-29, the building topped out in July 2025, and CHFA attended the grand opening on 2026-01-22. No placed-in-service or 8609 record was found.

next_step: Watch for CHFA records of the placed-in-service year and final credit amounts (CHFA's 2026 report cites $2.2M of federal credit, above the 2022 award).

key_numbers.meaning: 5 at 20% AMI, 20 at 30%, 29 at 50%, 17 at 60% and 31 at 80%; mostly one-bedrooms.

key_numbers.value: $1,934,593 a year federal 4% credit plus $1,000,000 state credit (2022 award)
key_numbers.meaning: CHFA's February 2026 report says it supported the project with $2.2M of federal 4% credit and $23.5M of bonds.
A $4M Denver HOST loan and $100,000 climate grant, plus $1M from the Proposition 123 Concessionary Debt LIHTC Gap Finance program.
Through ULC's community land trust and ground lease.

facts.value: Last parcel of ULC's 2-acre Mile High Vista site (former Festival Plaza parking lot), sharing a zone lot with the Corky Gonzales branch library and Del Norte's Avondale Apartments
Seven stories: concrete podium with about 38 covered parking spaces, leasing, community room and bike storage, then six residential floors; rooftop deck; CMX-12 zoning
All-electric with heat pumps, rooftop solar and EV charging; built to exceed NGBS
RTD 16 bus on the block; Decatur-Federal and Knox light rail stations on the W Line within half a mile; in a Qualified Census Tract
Universal design; transit passes for all residents (per CHFA's award description)

money.note: CHFA's February 2026 impact report cites $2.2 million of federal 4% credit.
The application planned a Freddie Mac tax-exempt loan with Wells Fargo as seller-servicer: $24.7M construction ($19.4M tax-exempt, $5.3M taxable) and $10.2M permanent.

money.source: Proposition 123 Concessionary Debt LIHTC Gap Finance
Denver Department of Housing Stability loan
Denver Office of Climate Action, Sustainability and Resiliency grant

money.note: ULC also planned to defer almost 40% of its developer fee.

parties.role: Property manager (ULC's manager per application; not confirmed for this building)
parties.name: Syringa Property Management

background.text: ULC bought the 2-plus-acre Festival Plaza parking lot for $2.1M (about $25 per sq ft) using the Denver TOD Fund, completed brownfield remediation and infrastructure by 2013, and served as master developer for Avondale Apartments (2014) and the Corky Gonzales library (2015).
Earlier plans for the last parcel (co-op, condos, middle-income rentals) did not proceed; ULC decided to develop permanently affordable rentals itself, its first ground-up housing development.
The 2022 application kept gas for central domestic hot water with electric PTACs; the finished building is described as all-electric with heat pumps.
The application requested a cost basis waiver and used steel construction to reach seven stories without triggering high-rise costs.
No asterisk footnote applies to this row in the award report; its asterisks only key the Type and Target codes.

discrepancies.text: The 2022 award report shows $1,934,593 a year of federal credit and $19,400,000 of bonds, while CHFA's February 2026 report says it supported the project with $2.2 million of federal 4% credit and $23.5 million of bonds.
The application says ULC bought the site in 2011, while ULC's 2024 release and the opening announcement say 2010.
Mile High CRE dates the topping-out celebration to July 24, 2025, while Colorado Construction & Design says July 30, 2025.

open_questions: Why and when the federal credit and bond amounts rose above the 2022 award (supplemental allocation or re-sizing).
